teaser: What do you build when no one hands you the plans? You are a 22, the number called the Master Builder, and an ISTJ, the type built for holding the line so everything else can function. The crossing is specific: a number that asks for structures large enough to outlast you, carried by a mind that trusts the next concrete step more than the far horizon. What is particular here is scale meeting caution — vision measured out in load-bearing increments, ambition that insists on checking the foundation twice before it will admit the building is real.
